title: Cover inequalities that tighten budget rows

questions.heading: A Cover Is a Set of Items That Cannot All Fit
questions.stem: A budget row reads 4a + 3b + 3c + 1d <= 8, with a, b, c and d binary. Which row is a valid cover inequality for it?

options.text: a + b + c <= 2, since a, b and c together cost 10
options.says: Right: 4 + 3 + 3 = 10 is more than 8, so no whole plan takes all three, and at most |C| - 1 = 2 of them.

options.text: a + b + d <= 2, since a, b and d together cost 8
options.says: A cover must cost more than the capacity; 8 fits within 8, so a whole plan may take a, b and d, and this row would cut it off.

options.text: a + b + c <= 1, since a, b and c together cost 10
options.says: The right side of a cover row is |C| - 1 = 2: b and c together cost 6 and fit, and this row would forbid them.

options.text: a + d <= 1, since a and d together cost 5
options.says: 5 fits within 8, so {a, d} is not a cover and both may be funded.

questions.heading: Shrink a Cover to Minimal, Then Extend It With Heavier Items
questions.stem: A row reads 6a + 5b + 4c + 4d + 2e <= 12. The cover {b, c, d} weighs 13 and gives b + c + d <= 2. Which items outside it may join the left side with the right side kept at 2?

options.text: a only, as it weighs at least as much as the cover's heaviest item
options.says: Right: any three of a, b, c, d weigh at least 4 + 4 + 5 = 13, more than 12, so the extended row a + b + c + d <= 2 is valid.

options.text: e only, as the lightest item barely moves the row's total
options.says: With e on the left, the plan b, c, e (weight 11) fits the budget but breaks the row; only items at least as heavy as the heaviest in the cover may join.

options.text: a and e, as every item outside the cover may join it freely
options.says: e may not join: b, c and e weigh 11 and fit, so a row allowing only two of them would cut off a whole plan.

options.text: neither, as a cover row's left side is fixed by its cover
options.says: The extended cover adds every item at least as heavy as the cover's heaviest, with the same right side.

questions.heading: Finding the Most Violated Cover Is a Knapsack of Its Own
questions.stem: At an LP point, items p and q are at 1 and item r is at 0.5, and {p, q, r} is a cover of the budget row. Is the cover row of {p, q, r} broken at that point?

options.text: No, since 1 + 1 + 0.5 stays below the 3 items of the cover
options.says: The right side is |C| - 1 = 2, not |C|; 2.5 is above it.

options.text: Yes, since 1 - x summed over the cover gives 0.5, below 1
options.says: Right: the cover row reads sum (1 - x_i) >= 1, and 0 + 0 + 0.5 is below 1.

options.text: That depends on the weights of p, q and r, not only on x
options.says: Once the set is a cover, its row is sum x_i <= |C| - 1, which has no weights; only the LP values decide.

options.text: No, since every LP point satisfies every valid inequality
options.says: A cut is exactly a valid inequality some LP point breaks, as x_P001 + x_P004 <= 1 was for tiny's LP point.
